extracted.intended_audience: Variety readers; entertainment/TV news consumers; fans and industry watchers interested in SNL, comedy casting, and celebrity interviews
extracted.subtask_description: A short-form entertainment news article reporting on a comedian's interview and reactions about his departure from a television sketch show, with context about casting and show decisions. Focus is on quoting the subject, summarizing claims, and situating them within broader show trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't pigeonhole performers ('impression box')
rubrics_metrics.description: Performers should not be put into boxes and limited to narrowly defined roles (e.g., being asked to do all the black impressions on the show).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use performers' full range of talents rather than confining them to a single type of bit or impression; avoid expectations that someone will always perform only a subset of roles. Anti-patterns include repeatedly casting the same performer only for certain demographic-specific parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect performers' boundaries — allow them to decline bits
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedians should be able to say no to particular bits (example: refusing to wear a dress) without being punished for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers and directors should not pressure talent into uncomfortable or demeaning assignments; honoring refusals preserves trust and can prevent conflict or loss of talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize meaningful recurring characters and impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows should maintain and use recurring characters/impressions (e.g., continuing Obama sketches) rather than abandoning them, as these showcase a performer’s strengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a performer has a signature impression or character, integrate it into programming rather than sidelining it; dropping such material can waste talent and fan interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-reliance on celebrity cameos
rubrics_metrics.description: Heavy use of A-list celebrity cameos can displace regular cast members and reduce opportunities for in-house talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance guest appearances with showcasing ensemble members so that the show develops and uses its own performers rather than substituting celebrities for character-driven comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve cast diversity and respond to concerns about representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Casting should actively include underrepresented groups (example: hiring more black female comedians) and producers should take diversity concerns seriously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address systemic gaps proactively rather than reactively; failure to diversify can lead to public criticism and internal tensions (the article references near-firing after speaking up about lack of African-American women).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster open but respectful dialogue with show leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Cast members can be assertive and raise issues (e.g., about diversity or creative use) while maintaining professional relationships with showrunners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive criticism should be allowed, and leadership should tolerate frank feedback without retaliatory action, preserving both morale and creative input.
